Paper: Introduction to Information Retrieval (textbook, Ch. 16.3, cluster purity)
MathematicalDefinition: purity(cluster_k) = max_j(count of class j in cluster k) / (size of cluster k); corpus purity = size-weighted mean over clusters.
OperatesOnHistoricalLabels: No (compares one clustering solution to ground-truth classes at one point in time, not repeated historical labels)
MultipleOrgsOrRatersInvolved: No (single ground-truth labeling vs. single clustering, not a multi-rater construct)
EquivalenceToADS: Equivalent (identical closed-form expression, max-count/total-count, under a relabeling of 'cluster' as 'item's historical booking multiset')
UsedAs: Evaluation metric only (post-hoc scoring of clustering output against known classes)
KeyNotes: Canonical textbook citation for the purity formula; formula reproduced identically across many independent secondary sources.
VerificationMethod: Formula confirmed via WebSearch cross-check against multiple independent course/paper citations reproducing the identical formula.

Paper: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Observer Error-Rates Using the EM Algorithm
Venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C (Applied Statistics)
DOI_or_URL: (2069 citations per Consensus; no DOI independently resolved in this pass)
MathematicalDefinition: EM-based latent-class model estimating per-rater confusion matrices and per-item true-label posteriors from repeated noisy categorical ratings; raw majority-vote-of-repeated-labels is the standard naive baseline compared against throughout this model's large descendant literature, though not itself named/defined as a standalone metric in this paper.
UnitOfAnalysis: Per-item (task), aggregating multiple raters' repeated labels -- the closest unit-of-analysis match to ADS found in this pass
OperatesOnHistoricalLabels: Yes -- this is the one line of literature that operates on exactly ADS's data shape: repeated categorical judgments of the same item
EquivalenceToADS: Analogous (unit of analysis and data shape match exactly; but Dawid-Skene's own output is a corrected posterior, not the raw max/sum -- the mathematically-identical quantity is only its baseline comparator, used informally, never named as a citable metric in its own right)
UsedAs: Model itself: label aggregation / ground-truth (truth) inference. Majority-vote-proportion within this lineage: naive baseline for comparison, occasionally a worker/task quality diagnostic.
KeyNotes: Strongest evidence that 'empirical historical label determinism' as ADS defines it is a known baseline quantity in the repeated-labeling literature, circulating informally rather than under one canonical citable name.
VerificationMethod: Retrieved via Consensus with full bibliographic metadata; cross-referenced against multiple descendant papers (Zhang et al. 2016 GTIC; Gao and Zhou 2013) that explicitly cite and benchmark against it.

MathematicalDefinition: Frames per-item label distributions (not reduced to a point estimate) as the object of study; discusses soft labels, entropy of the label distribution, and majority/aggregated hard labels as competing representations of ground truth per item.
OperatesOnHistoricalLabels: Yes (annotation-repetition sense; mathematically identical shape to ADS's booking-history repetition, though not longitudinal)
EquivalenceToADS: Analogous ('how peaked is an item's label distribution' is the same conceptual territory as ADS, but the survey's emphasis is on NOT collapsing to a point estimate -- closer to the opposite design philosophy from ADS-Cascade, which deliberately collapses to a scalar routing signal)

Paper: Confident Learning: Estimating Uncertainty in Dataset Labels
MathematicalDefinition: Estimates the joint distribution between noisy given labels and latent true labels via out-of-sample model-predicted class probabilities and per-class probability thresholds; flags/prunes likely label errors via confident-joint / self-confidence thresholding.
UnitOfAnalysis: Per-example, scored via a trained model's predicted probability for the given label -- NOT via repeated historical labels
OperatesOnHistoricalLabels: No -- uses a single given label per example plus model-predicted probabilities, not a repeated-labeling history
MultipleOrgsOrRatersInvolved: No -- single label source, single trained model as the confidence oracle
EquivalenceToADS: Distinct (different input: model confidence vs. repeated empirical labels; different mechanism: probabilistic confusion-matrix estimation vs. simple counting -- though the goal, identifying unreliable/ambiguous items, is convergent with ADS's downstream use)
UsedAs: Dataset-quality / label-error-detection tool; used as a data-cleaning preprocessing step (dataset characteristic), not an architecture-selection or routing signal
KeyNotes: 61 citations; companion paper 'Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize ML Benchmarks' (Northcutt, Athalye, Mueller 2021) cross-referenced.
VerificationMethod: FastTrack metadata confirmed (JAIR, OpenAlex-backed); cross-referenced against companion arXiv paper.

Paper: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks (MSP)
MathematicalDefinition: confidence(x) = max_k softmax(f(x))_k -- the maximum predicted class probability from a trained model's softmax output for a single input.
OperatesOnHistoricalLabels: No -- operates on a model's predictive distribution for one forward pass, not repeated empirical labels over time
EquivalenceToADS: Distinct, but structurally analogous (both are literally max(distribution) over classes -- but MSP maxes a MODEL'S predictive distribution at inference time; ADS maxes an EMPIRICAL HISTORICAL FREQUENCY distribution computed independent of any model; same operator, categorically different input data)
UsedAs: Runtime confidence/OOD-detection baseline -- notably this IS a runtime signal, just not built from repeated historical labels
KeyNotes: Cleanest illustration in the search of 'same operator, different input data'; worth citing in the manuscript precisely as a contrast, not a match. 1629 citations.
VerificationMethod: get_paper confirmed DOI, authors, venue, citation count directly.

Paper: Measuring Nominal Scale Agreement Among Many Raters
DOI_or_URL: (no DOI independently resolved in this pass; canonical IRR methodology citation)
MathematicalDefinition: Fleiss's kappa; the per-item term P_i = [sum_j C(n_ij,2)] / C(n,2) -- fraction of AGREEING PAIRS of ratings for item i (not fraction agreeing with the mode). Raw/percent agreement and 'percent agreement with the majority label' are related-but-distinct informal constructs discussed in this lineage without their own dedicated citation.
EquivalenceToADS: Partially equivalent, with an important distinction: Fleiss's own P_i (pairwise-agreement fraction) is Analogous, not equivalent, to ADS (mathematically different: pairwise agreement vs. max/sum, converging only under specific distributional conditions). The informal 'percent agreement with the majority label' construct that circulates in this literature IS mathematically Equivalent to ADS, but has no single canonical, independently-named citation distinct from Cohen's/Fleiss's kappa work.
UsedAs: Evaluation metric / dataset (annotator) quality diagnostic in inter-rater-reliability methodology
KeyNotes: Most important 'near miss': the raw majority-agreement-proportion really does appear to lack a canonical distinct citation lineage separate from kappa, exactly as the task's framing anticipated.
